name: aws-roles-anywhere
summary: AWS for the agent without a stored key: a certificate on this machine, 1-hour credentials in the sandbox (IAM Roles Anywhere), a read-only role and a deploy role

requires.aws: AWS CLI v2, signed in with admin rights on the target account (used once, here, never in the sandbox): https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/getting-started-install.html

args.help: AWS CLI profile with admin rights on the target account, used here to set it up (not given to the agent)
AWS region of the agent's work, e.g. us-east-1
prefix of the AWS resources' names (default briefling-agent-)
extra tag KEY=VALUE on the AWS resources (repeatable)
CDK bootstrap stack to fix for the deploy role (default CDKToolkit)
leave the CDK bootstrap alone (no cdk deploy then)

steps.why: AWS's official aws_signing_helper trades the certificate for 1-hour credentials.
steps.risk: a binary from rolesanywhere.amazonaws.com, at a pinned version, refused unless its SHA-256 is the one AWS publishes.

steps.what: Certificate authority and the agent's certificate
steps.why: The agent's identity: the CA is made once per machine, the certificate (CN = the agent's name) is valid one year and renewed by running this again.
steps.risk: the private keys stay in ~/.config/briefling-agent (mode 600), never in the sandbox: whoever reads them gets the agent's AWS access.

steps.why: A trust anchor for the CA, a 1-hour profile, a read role (ReadOnlyAccess without secret values) and a deploy role that may only enter the CDK bootstrap roles.
steps.risk: creates IAM roles in the account with your admin profile; the stack and its names say {prefix}{name}.

steps.why: Roles Anywhere carries the agent's name (source identity) through every role it enters: the CDK roles must accept it, else cdk deploy is refused.
steps.risk: changes the trust of the bootstrap roles towards this account only; the change set is shown and refused if it replaces anything. A later standard `cdk bootstrap` removes it: run this again.

service.why: aws_signing_helper serve hands out the 1-hour credentials like an EC2 instance's metadata endpoint, renewed before they expire.
service.risk: it has no password: any program of this machine can read the agent's 1-hour credentials on that port.

vm.why: The sandbox's commands find the credentials service (default = the read role), and a `deploy` profile for cdk deploy.

install: set -e; cd /tmp; curl -fsSL -o awscliv2.zip "https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-$(uname -m).zip"; unzip -q -o awscliv2.zip; sudo ./aws/install --update; rm -rf aws awscliv2.zip
needs.what: AWS CLI v2 in the sandbox
